title: Docs IA for Quickstart templates: “Choose your template” + “Production checklist” sections
creator: Talia Benson
content:
## Context
We’re launching a set of production-minded Quickstart templates (RAG, agents, combined) with a consistent telemetry + safe-defaults contract. Docs needs a clear, low-friction landing experience that:
- gets users to the right template fast (“Choose your template”)
- sets expectations on production-grade defaults (“Production checklist”)
- maps cleanly to Hosted API + Console capabilities (cost/latency, request IDs, fallbacks, rollouts)
- avoids unsafe patterns (secrets, PII, tool calling)

This ticket covers the docs-site information architecture (IA) + page layout recommendations for the Quickstart templates area.

## Problem statement
Current docs navigation is organized by feature and API surface area, but templates are a workflow-based onramp. Without a dedicated IA, users will:
- pick the wrong template (e.g., start with Agents when they just need RAG)
- miss key operational guidance (timeouts/retries, 429 behavior, telemetry setup)
- treat the quickstart as toy code and hit support issues on day 1

## Scope
Design the IA + layout for:
1) Quickstart templates landing page
2) “Choose your template” section (template picker)
3) “Production checklist” section (sane defaults + required ops hooks)

Deliverable is a written spec + layout wireframe guidance (no pixel-perfect UI required) suitable for Docs + DevEx to implement in the docs site.

## Non-goals
- Full visual redesign of docs site.
- Creating new product UX in Console.
- Writing full doc copy (Docs team owns final copy, this provides structure and key callouts).

## Constraints / requirements
- Must work for both self-serve PLG users and enterprise evaluators.
- Must minimize cognitive load: pick a template in <30 seconds.
- Must make “production shape” defaults obvious without overwhelming new users.
- Must accommodate 3 templates at launch:
  - RAG service + ingestion
  - Agents + tool calling
  - Combined RAG + agent workflow
- Should leave room for future expansion (language variants, backends, “advanced” templates).
- Should align with telemetry contract messaging: request_id correlation, tenant IDs, model/route tags, token usage/cost, error taxonomy.

## Proposed IA (recommended)
### Navigation placement
Add top-level docs nav entry (or prominent section under “Guides”):
- Guides → Quickstart templates

### Page set
1) /quickstarts (Landing)
2) /quickstarts/rag
3) /quickstarts/agents
4) /quickstarts/rag-agent
5) /quickstarts/production-checklist (optional standalone; also embedded section on landing)

Rationale: landing enables fast selection; per-template pages keep walkthroughs focused; checklist can be referenced in multiple places (and from repo README).

## Layout spec
### Landing page: above-the-fold
- Title: “Quickstart templates”
- One-sentence value prop: “Go from API key to a working, observable app in <15 minutes.”
- Two primary CTAs:
  1) “Choose a template” (anchor to template picker)
  2) “See production checklist” (anchor)
- Small note under CTAs: deployment modes supported (Hosted now; Dedicated/Private path documented).

### Section 1: Choose your template (template picker)
Use a 3-card layout (responsive grid). Each card must include:
- Template name (RAG / Agents / RAG + Agents)
- One-line “best for”
- What you get (bullets, max 3)
- Key integration callouts (badges)
  - “OpenTelemetry”
  - “Request IDs”
  - “Streaming” (if applicable)
  - “Docker Compose”
  - “Kubernetes manifests”
- Effort/time estimate (e.g., “~15 min local, ~60 min deploy”)
- Primary action: “Open template”
- Secondary action: “View repo” (or “GitHub”)

Add a lightweight comparison table below the cards (optional) for users who want more detail:
Columns: Template | When to use | Includes ingestion? | Tool calling? | Default backend | Language options | Deployment artifacts

Decision guidance copy (short, directly above cards):
- “If you’re not sure, start with RAG.”
- “If you need tool execution, choose Agents.”
- “If you need both knowledge + actions, choose RAG + Agents.”

### Section 2: Production checklist
This must be scannable and not read like a security policy document. Recommend a checklist grouped into 4 categories with collapsible details:

A) Reliability defaults (visible bullets)
- Timeouts set (connect + read)
- Retries with backoff + jitter (safe defaults; respect Retry-After)
- 429 handling guidance
- Graceful shutdown + in-flight request drain
- Health/readiness endpoints

B) Observability (visible bullets)
- OpenTelemetry traces enabled
- Structured logs with request_id + tenant correlation
- Cost/latency metrics emitted (token usage, time to first token)
- Error taxonomy (timeout vs upstream vs validation)
- “See in Console” deep links example

C) Security & data handling (visible bullets)
- Secrets: no keys in repo; .env patterns; rotation note
- PII guidance + logging hygiene (don’t log prompts by default; redaction note)
- Tool calling guardrails (allow-list; tool timeouts; schema validation)
- CORS defaults / auth boundaries (for web templates)

D) Deployment path (visible bullets)
- Local dev (env + compose)
- Managed deploy (container/K8s)
- Dedicated/Private considerations (routing policies, audit logs, network boundaries)

Each category should include a “Why this matters” one-liner and link out to deeper docs (SDK retry guide, telemetry contract, secrets policy, tool calling guidelines).

### Optional: “What happens when things go wrong?” callout
Small callout box linking to:
- common errors (401 key issues, 404 model mismatch, 429 rate limits, streaming disconnects)
- expected behavior and where to look in Console (trace + error panel)

## Content/UX guidelines (for Docs implementation)
- Keep the landing page to ~1.5 screens before the fold on a laptop.
- Avoid walls of text; use progressive disclosure.
- Use consistent naming with repos (“redwood-quickstarts”) and template folders.
- Every section should end with an action (go to template, set up telemetry, deploy).

## Accessibility
- Cards must be keyboard navigable.
- Badge-only information must have text equivalents.
- Checklist sections must use semantic headings and proper list markup.

## Deliverables
- IA recommendation (this ticket)
- Wireframe-level layout notes for landing + two key sections
- Copy prompts (headings and placeholder text) to unblock Docs

## Acceptance criteria
- Docs can implement a landing page that clearly routes users to the right template.
- Production checklist is scannable in <2 minutes and links to deeper guides.
- Layout supports future expansion (new templates, languages, backends) without re-IA.

## Reviews / decisions
- 2025-12-12 (Wei Chen + Elliot Price): Prefer top-level “Quickstart templates” under Guides vs under API Reference. Keep “Choose your template” as a card picker (not a long list).
- 2025-12-13 (Monica Patel): Add explicit callout for retry/timeout defaults and streaming disconnect handling to reduce ticket volume.
- 2025-12-16 (Naomi Feldman): Ensure checklist includes a clear “don’t log prompts by default” note and tool allow-list requirement.

## Implementation notes (handoff)
- Docs PR should mirror this structure; final copy can be adjusted but keep card + checklist information hierarchy.
- If only one page can ship at launch, prioritize landing with anchored sections; per-template pages can be thinner initially.

## Links
- ENG-2850 Docs-site integration (implements this IA)
- Confluence PRD: PRD: quickstart templates (RAG + agents)

## Status updates
- 2025-12-18: Draft IA + section layout posted to Docs channel for feedback.
- 2026-01-07: Incorporated Security + SDK feedback; aligned terminology with “Hosted / Dedicated / Private.”
- 2026-01-10: Marked done; handed off to Docs for implementation in ENG-2850.
